svg.text: OAuth 2.0 / OIDC / SSO — Frontend LLD
OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE Flow
1. User clicks "Sign in with Google" → generate code_verifier (random 32 bytes)
2. code_challenge = BASE64URL(SHA256(code_verifier)) → store verifier in sessionStorage
3. Redirect to /authorize?response_type=code&client_id&redirect_uri&scope&code_challenge
4. IdP authenticates user → redirects back with ?code=AUTH_CODE&state=NONCE
5. Verify state === sessionStorage nonce (CSRF protection)
6. POST /token: {code, code_verifier, redirect_uri} → {access_token, id_token, refresh_token}
7. Validate id_token JWT: sig, iss, aud, exp, nonce — extract user claims
8. Store access_token in memory only; refresh_token in httpOnly cookie via BFF
Token Lifecycle & Silent Refresh
• Access token: short-lived (15–60 min), stored in-memory (React context/Zustand)
• Refresh token: long-lived (days), stored in httpOnly Secure SameSite=Strict cookie
• Silent refresh: POST /token with grant_type=refresh_token (via BFF, no JS access)
• Proactive refresh: schedule refresh 60s before expiry using exp claim from JWT
• Refresh token rotation: IdP issues new refresh token on each use (detect replay)
• Token interception: Axios/fetch interceptor queues concurrent requests during refresh
• Failed refresh → clear state → redirect to /login with returnUrl preserved
• Cross-tab sync: BroadcastChannel propagates token refresh / logout to all tabs
Enterprise SSO (SAML / OIDC Federation)
• SP-initiated SAML: redirect to IdP → SAML assertion POST back to ACS URL
• OIDC federation: IdP discovery via .well-known/openid-configuration endpoint
• Email-based IdP routing: extract domain → map to tenant IdP config
• JIT provisioning: create user on first SSO login from SAML attributes/OIDC claims
• Session bridging: SSO session lifetime ≠ app session — track both independently
• Global logout (SLO): receive logout request from IdP → invalidate local session
• Attribute mapping: SAML attributes → app roles/permissions via claim transformations
• Multi-IdP: support Google, Okta, Azure AD — abstract behind AuthProvider interface
Security, Scopes & Edge Cases
• PKCE mandatory for SPAs (replaces client_secret for public clients)
• state parameter: random nonce stored in sessionStorage, verified on callback
• Scope negotiation: request minimal scopes (openid profile email), incremental auth
• Consent screen: show requested scopes, allow partial grant, handle scope_denied
• Token binding: bind access token to client TLS cert (mTLS) for high-security apps
• Edge: popup vs redirect — popup breaks on mobile; use redirect with returnUrl param
• id_token nonce: embed nonce in auth request, verify in id_token to prevent replay
• Clock skew: allow ±60s leeway when validating exp/iat claims in id_token
PKCE: code_verifier → SHA256 → BASE64URL
Access token: in-memory only (not localStorage)
Silent refresh: 60s before exp, queue concurrent reqs
SSO: email domain → IdP routing → JIT provision
SLO: IdP logout → invalidate all local sessions
